 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C. V. Bhaskar Reddy

entities.text: Habeeba Sultana vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Writ Petition No.20535 of 2023
Order:

This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed by the petitioner, seeking the following relief:
"....to issue a writ, Order or Direction(s) particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the highhanded action of the Respondents in taking over possession of the land from petitioner to an extent of Ac.0- 15 Guntas in Sy.No.248/I and aiso an extent of land in Ac.0.09 Gts in Sy.No.250/U, totalling Ac.0- 24 Gts,
situated at Chengole Village, Tandur Mandal, Vikarabad District for the formation of Tandur bypass road, in pursuance of the Notice dated 26.10.2017 vide Proceedings No.B/120/2017, issued under Section 21 of the Act No.30 of 2013, without following due process of law as illegal and arbitrary resulting in violation of Article 14, 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India and set aside the same and consequently direct the Respondents to follow due process of law..."

2. It is the case of the petitioner that she is the owner and possessor of land admeasuring Ac.1.00 gts in Sy.No.248 and Ac.1.33 gts in Sy.No.250 situated at Chengole Village, Tandur Mandal, Vikarabad District, having purchased the same under registered sale deeds dated 30.05.1996, 06.05.1996 and 23.12.1999.

It is further case of the petitioner that for the purpose of formation of Tandur by- pass road from KM 0/0 to 12/0 KMS, the respondents have issued preliminary notification dated 03.07.2017 under Section 11 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short "the Act") and thereafter, issued notice dated 25.11.2017 under Section 21 of the Act.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is the case of the petitioner that she participated in the award enquiry and requested to pay compensation basing on the market value of commercial land i.e, per square yard basis.

However, the respondents, through a Negotiation Committee, determined compensation of Rs.15 lakhs and Rs.18 lakhs per acre for agricultural land,
which she disagreed with.

It is further case of the petitioner that despite submitting representations on 07.06.2021 and 31.05.2023, seeking compensation based on market value per square yard, no action has been taken by the respondents.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the respondents are attempting to take possession of the petitioner's property without paying adequate compensation as required under the provisions of the Act.
It is argued that even though the petitioner has submitted representations dated 07.06.2021 and 31.05.2023 to the respondents, till date, the respondents have not taken any action.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for the respondents submitted that acquisition of the petitioner's land was initiated as part of the project for formation of Tandur bypass road from KM 0/0 to 12/0 Kms.

It is further submitted that the preliminary notification was published in the Telangana Gazette on 03.07.2017 and no objections were received under Section 15(1) of the Act within the time stipulated.
The petitioner participated in the award enquiry and raised objection regarding the classification of the land, and refused to give consent in Form E-1.
As such, the award was not passed in respect of the petitioner's land and possession was not handed over to the requisition authorities.

5. In view of the above submissions, as the petitioner has raised objections concerning the classification of her land as agricultural land and requested to pay compensation basing on the market value applicable to commercial lands and further, as the award has not yet been passed by the respondent No.2 and possession of the land was also not taken, this Court deems it appropriate to direct the respondent No.2 to consider the representations dated 07.06.2021 and 31.05.2023 submitted by the petitioner in terms of Section 23 of the Act and pass appropriate orders, in accordance with law, within a period of eight (8) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
6. With the above observations, the writ petition is disposed of.
No order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
No order as to costs.
__ C.V. BHASKAR REDDY, J Date: 11.09.2024 scs Mrs. Habeeba Sultana vs The State Of Telangana on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194039414/
